newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST--Dlr/mark to commence decline end Q1 '97.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST--Dlr/mark to commence decline end Q1 '97.

text.p: Dollar/mark could still make fresh new highs in the near term, but market economists predicted the rally will derail by March and the dollar will decline gradually through the rest of 1997.

The dollar could extend its string of new highs in the coming weeks, propelled by expectations of higher rates in the U.S. and lower rates in Germany. But the sustainability of dollar/mark's advance is in question, said economists polled for the latest Reuters quarterly U.S. economic survey.

"I think the economy is going to slow down here and I don't think things are as bad in Europe as people think," said Earl Johnson, foreign exchange economist at Bank of Montreal in Chicago. "It could be a month or two before that happens and in that interim we could spike a lot higher."

Economists, on average, forecast the dollar will fall to 1.6252 marks, below its late-Tuesday exchange rate of about 1.6530 marks, by the end of the first quarter and to decline steadily to 1.5930 by year's end, according to a quarterly survey conducted by Reuters between January 21 and 23.

Johnson said he thinks the market will eventually be disappointed on the interest rate front. He predicted the Federal Reserve will fail to raise interest rates and major European central banks will not ease credit.
Economists also said that investors, always sensitive to U.S. trade deficits, will begin to worry that the dollar's strength will cut into U.S. exports.
"Once again there will be a focus on our large current account imbalance and that will move the currency lower," said Cary Leahey, senior economist at Lehman Government Securities Inc.
"To plug that gap you need some decline in the purchasing power of the dollar to make our goods more competitive," he added.
Average forecasts place the dollar at 1.6229 marks at the end of the second quarter of this year, and at 1.6014 marks by the end of September.
The 27 first-quarter forecasts ranged from a high projection of 1.70 marks by Goldman Sachs to HSBC Securities' low call of 1.48 marks.
The spectrum of year-end predictions, numbering 26, was wider. They ran from 1.43 marks by the Conference Board at the low end, to 1.73 marks, where ABN-AMRO Bank represented the top.
